title: Taxable Fixed Income Markets Update: September 2026
summary: Higher rates challenged fixed income markets in September, but the move also pushed yields higher. From historically tight corporate spreads to resilient shorter-duration asset-backed securities, explore the trends shaping fixed income markets.

# Taxable Fixed Income Markets Update: September 2026


[Douglas Gimple](https://www.diamond-hill.com/about/our-people/douglas-gimple/)


13 October 2026


---


September’s sharp rise in interest rates weighed on fixed income markets, with longer-duration sectors bearing the brunt of the selloff even as higher yields improved the income outlook for investors. Shifting economic and inflation data continued to reshape fixed income conditions.


**Treasury and rates** . Treasury yields rose sharply in September, with the two-year yield climbing 55 basis points, the 10-year yield rising 54 basis points and the 30-year yield increasing 39 basis points. Stronger economic data, persistent inflation concerns, elevated energy prices, heavy Treasury and corporate issuance, fiscal uncertainty and the Federal Reserve’s first rate increase since summer 2023 contributed to the move. Longer-term Treasury yields reached levels not seen since before the financial crisis.1


**Corporate credit** . Investment grade corporate spreads widened modestly but remained near historically tight levels. The Bloomberg US Corporate Index returned -2.72% in September as higher Treasury yields pressured prices, while yield to worst increased to 6.04%. Longer-duration securities generally fared worse. September investment grade corporate issuance reached $197 billion, 33% above the four-year September average, while high yield issuance rose to a 12-month high.1,2


**Securitized** . Duration also drove performance across securitized markets. Shorter-duration asset-backed securities held up comparatively well, returning -0.96%, while agency residential mortgage-backed securities fell 3.38% and spreads widened materially. Commercial mortgage-backed securities spreads moved slightly wider. Issuance remained strong: year-to-date asset-backed securities issuance reached $284 billion, non-agency commercial mortgage-backed securities supply reached $133 billion and single asset/single borrower issuance climbed to $75 billion. Non-agency residential mortgage-backed securities issuance slowed but remained on pace to exceed prior-year levels.1,3
